                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"Docling (v2 CPU build, `docling` importable from the system Python, every model weight already baked into the image's local artifact cache) can reconstruct the grid of a table it finds on a PDF page, and its table-structure recognizer exposes two operating modes with different speed/quality trade-offs.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'A data-engineering team needs hard numbers before choosing a mode for production: how much quality does the slower mode actually buy on their documents, and how much runtime does it cost? Your job is to build the measurement harness that answers this, scored against a ground-truth corpus that ships with the environment.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**The harness must work fully offline.** No network call, external service or model download may be required at run time - everything comes from local resources - and the whole run must fit inside a 3 GB memory limit.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## The corpus (read-only input)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The corpus lives at `/home/user/tfbench/corpus`. You must not modify, move, delete or regenerate any file in it.\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +

                [32m'  "tables": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'    {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "table_index": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "page_no": 1,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "num_rows": 5,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "num_cols": 4,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "cells": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'        {"row": 0, "col": 0, "row_span": 1, "col_span": 1, "text": "Region", "is_header": true}\n'[39m +
                [32m'      ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Build a reproducible benchmark CLI at `/home/user/tfbench/bench.py` that, for each selected document, converts the PDF **once per selected table-structure mode** using the real recognizer (never a heuristic re-parse of the PDF, and never the ground truth), extracts the recognized grids, scores them against the ground truth, and writes JSON reports.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The two modes must be reported under the exact names `fast` and `accurate`, and both must run with table cell-matching enabled.\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Interface\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +

A ground-truth table with no counterpart is scored as a total miss (no recognized shape, zero agreements). Recognized tables beyond the ground-truth count are only counted, not scored.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"**Cell probing**: a ground-truth cell at (`row`, `col`) is compared with the recognized cell that covers grid position (`row`, `col`) in the paired recognized table — i.e. the cell whose row range and column range both contain that position; if several do, the first one in the recognized table's own cell order wins. If no recognized cell covers the position (including when the recognized grid is smaller), the probe has no recognized counterpart: its recognized text, span and header flag are all `null` and none of its three agreements hold.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Per-cell agreements**: content matches when the normalized texts are equal (two empty strings match); the span matches when (`row_span`, `col_span`) are pairwise equal; the header flag matches when the ground-truth `is_header` equals whether the recognized table marks that cell as a column-header cell.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"**Per-table metrics**: `matched_cells`, `span_agreements` and `header_agreements` are the counts of the corresponding agreements over the ground-truth cells of that table; each rate is that count divided by the table's ground-truth cell count. `shape_match` is true only when the recognized row count and column count both equal the ground-truth ones.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Aggregation**: corpus-level rates are micro-averaged — the summed agreement counts over all scored tables divided by the summed ground-truth cell count — never the mean of per-table rates. `shape_match_rate` is the number of shape-matching tables divided by the ground-truth table count of the run.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Rounding**: every rate and every duration written to JSON is a float; rates are rounded to 4 decimals and durations to 3 decimals. A rate whose denominator is 0 is `0.0`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Quality gate**: `best_mode` is the selected mode with the highest corpus-level `cell_match_rate` (on a tie, `fast`); `best_cell_match_rate` is its rate. The gate passes when `best_cell_match_rate` is greater than or equal to `0.5`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Output files (all under `--out`)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`docs/<doc_id>.json`, one per selected document:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "doc_id": "string",\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "pdf": "string",\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "gt_table_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "gt_cell_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "modes": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "fast": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "mode": "fast",\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "cell_matching": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "converted": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "error": null,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "predicted_table_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "unmatched_predicted_tables": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "tables": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'        {\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "table_index": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "page_no": 1,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "gt_shape": [0, 0],\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "pred_shape": [0, 0],\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "shape_match": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "pred_page_no": 1,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "pred_bbox": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "gt_cell_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "matched_cells": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "cell_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "span_agreements": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "span_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "header_agreements": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "header_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'          "cells": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'            {\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "row": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "col": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "gt_text_normalized": "string",\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "pred_text_normalized": "string",\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "matched": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "gt_span": [1, 1],\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "pred_span": [1, 1],\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "span_match": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "gt_header": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "pred_header": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'              "header_match": true\n'[39m +
                [32m'            }\n'[39m +
                [32m'          ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'        }\n'[39m +
                [32m'      ]\n'[39m +
                [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"`modes` holds exactly the modes that were run. `error` is `null` on success and otherwise a non-empty string describing the failure, with `converted` false and `tables` still listing every ground-truth table as a total miss. `pred_shape` is `[rows, cols]` or `null`; `pred_page_no` is the 1-based page of the recognized table or `null`; `pred_bbox` is the recognized table's bounding box as `[left, top, right, bottom]` in page coordinates rounded to 2 decimals, or `null`. `tables` is ordered by `table_index` and `cells` by (`row`, `col`) ascending.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`aggregate.json`:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "corpus_dir": "corpus",\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "doc_ids": ["string"],\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "doc_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "gt_table_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "gt_cell_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "modes": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "fast": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "mode": "fast",\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "cell_matching": true,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "documents_run": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "documents_converted": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "documents_failed": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "predicted_table_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "shape_match_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "shape_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "matched_cells": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "cell_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "span_agreements": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "span_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "header_agreements": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "header_match_rate": 0.0\n'[39m +
                [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "best_mode": "fast",\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "best_cell_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "quality_gate": {"min_cell_match_rate": 0.5, "passed": true}\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`corpus_dir` is the corpus path exactly as it was given on the command line (or its default). `doc_ids` is sorted ascending.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`comparison.json` — written **only** when both modes ran:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'```json\n'[39m +
                [32m'{\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "modes": ["fast", "accurate"],\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "tables": [\n'[39m +
                [32m'    {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "doc_id": "string",\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "table_index": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "fast_shape": [0, 0],\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "accurate_shape": [0, 0],\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "shape_differs": false,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "fast_cell_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "accurate_cell_match_rate": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "cell_match_rate_delta": 0.0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "differing_cells": [[0, 0]],\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "differing_cell_count": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'      "verdict": "tie"\n'[39m +
                [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ],\n'[39m +
                [32m'  "summary": {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "tables_compared": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "accurate_better": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "fast_better": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "tie": 0,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    "shape_differs_count": 0\n'[39m +
                [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                [32m'}\n'[39m +
                [32m'```\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"One entry per ground-truth table, ordered by (`doc_id`, `table_index`) ascending. `differing_cells` lists the (`row`, `col`) probes whose normalized recognized text differs between the two modes (a `null` differs from any string; two `null`s do not), sorted ascending; `cell_match_rate_delta` is the accurate rate minus the fast rate rounded to 4 decimals, and `verdict` is `accurate_better`, `fast_better` or `tie` according to that delta's sign.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'`timing.json` — this file is the only one exempt from the byte-identical requirement:\n'[39m +

            [32m'4. expectedReplacements: The number of replacements you expect to make. Defaults to 1 if not specified.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'By default, the tool will replace ONE occurrence of searchContent with replaceContent in the specified file. If you want to replace multiple occurrences, provide the expectedReplacements parameter with the exact number of occurrences you expect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. UNIQUENESS (when expectedReplacements is not specified): The searchContent MUST uniquely identify the specific instance you want to change. This means:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Include AT LEAST 3-5 lines of context BEFORE the change point\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Include AT LEAST 3-5 lines of context AFTER the change point\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Include all whitespace, indentation, and surrounding code exactly as it appears in the file\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. EXPECTED MATCHES: If you want to replace multiple instances:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Use the expectedReplacements parameter with the exact number of occurrences you expect to replace\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - This will replace ALL occurrences of the searchContent with the replaceContent\n'[39m +
            [32m"   - If the actual number of matches doesn't equal expectedReplacements, the edit will fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'   - This is a safety feature to prevent unintended replacements\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. VERIFICATION: Before using this tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response.             [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes.             [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m"- The tool will return the skill's instructions\n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- This is a BLOCKING REQUIREMENT: invoke the relevant Skill tool BEFORE generating any other response about a specific skill or task\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
